question: Can real recordings support a test of transferring an occurrence-specific external event between repetitions of the same Assembly101 task?
status: Exploratory feasibility screen fixed after inspecting the official fine/coarse schemas, one coarse label example and availability, before computing cross-role counts or baseline predictions.
sample: Use the publicly listed assembly_* coarse annotation files in the original authors' Google Drive embedded folder paired to the official fine validation.csv. Assembly actions only. Report exact coverage of the official fine split. No footage, poses or feature downloads.
unit: One physical sequence removes the /camera suffix. Deduplicate exact (sequence, start, end, verb, noun); simultaneous identically labeled actions indistinguishable in these timestamps collapse. A coarse role is its full official action name. Keep nonempty foreground actions uniquely strictly interior to one coarse interval (coarse_start < fine_start < fine_end < coarse_end), excluding background/idle coarse roles.
pairing: Require identical toy ID, assembly phase, different physical recordings and different participant IDs. Eligible fine action must occur under >=2 different coarse labels within each recording. Specific event is a (fine_verb,noun,coarse_role) combination occurring exactly once in each recording. Report ordered and unordered counts and distinct physical units; label occurrences within recorded state only, no simulator outcome.
baseline: For every eligible ordered source-target-role triple, give rank-only comparator the rank of the selected occurrence among admissible occurrences of that fine label in the source. Predict same ordinal in target (out-of-range is failure). Also report nearest normalized ordinal in target, ties to smaller index. Report pooled and per unordered pair averaged accuracy. This retrospective comparator uses the containment filter and normalized ordinal also uses the target count. An online model would need a distinct causal baseline. Chance is mean inverse eligible fine occurrence count in target. Also report a conservative subset where rank changes between source/target for diagnostic size only. No fitting.
limit: This screen establishes annotation-level feasibility and controlled variation; no claim of neural transfer, causal task success, unseen dataset generalization or independence of pairs sharing episodes.
